 Lakers sign new 7-foot center, waive forward in roster move 
 2026-10-28 21:34 
 The Lakers are signing 7-foot center Lawson Lovering to a two-way deal after his brief NBA stint with Memphis last season, while waiving forward AK Okereke to open the roster spot.
 Credit: AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix 
 Credit AP - Scanpix 
 Add us on 
 Add us on 
 The Los Angeles Lakers have agreed to a two-way contract with 7-foot center Lawson Lovering , according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype .

 To open a two-way roster spot, Los Angeles is waiving forward AK Okereke , who joined the Lakers after going undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft.
 Lovering, 23, already has NBA experience after appearing in two games for the Memphis Grizzlies last season. He averaged 7.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.5 assists in 24.5 minutes while shooting 60.0% from the field.
 His best NBA performance came against the Utah Jazz on Feb. 20, when he recorded 11 points, 11 rebounds, and three assists in 32 minutes.
 Lovering had originally earned his NBA opportunity through Memphis' G League system. The Grizzlies signed him to a 10-day contract in February after he spent most of the season with the Memphis Hustle.
 He later returned to Memphis on an Exhibit 10 deal before the 2026-27 season but was waived in late September when the Grizzlies signed Carson Cooper to a two-way contract.
 Lovering gives Lakers additional size
 Lovering went undrafted in 2025 after a four-year college career split between Colorado and Utah.
 The signing adds another natural center to a Lakers roster currently featuring Walker Kessler and Kevon Looney.
 Los Angeles had reportedly been exploring additional frontcourt options early in the season, with its two-way roster spots viewed as a potential avenue to add size.
 Lakers move on from AK Okereke
 Okereke's stint on the Lakers' two-way roster ends only a few months after he signed with the team.
 The 23-year-old forward went undrafted after spending his final college season at Vanderbilt, where he averaged 9.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.0 assists in 36 games while shooting 40.0% from the three-point range.
